alice: deploy-bot finished postdeploy smoke for rollout/2026-12-tokenizer-optim. quick flag: tokenizer service CPU climbs during prefill, causing short-lived enqueueing and p95 blips on /embed and /gen. :warning:
deploy-bot: POSTDEPLOY SMOKE REPORT for rollout/2026-12-tokenizer-optim
```
status: partial-pass
checks: [health, synth-prefill, tokenization-warmup]
tokenizer.cpu: baseline=22% -> observed=92% (3m spike)
embed.p95: baseline=115ms -> observed=260ms (10m window)
errors: small bump in 429s, no host OOMs reported
notes: spike coincides with kv-prefill + tokenizer shard warmup
```
sre-oncall: traces show long waits at tokenizer pool handoff (eu-west). no OOMs but high sys CPU on tokenizer pod. links: https://traces/internal/token/token-4567
ram: could be a faulty sharding config or a new tensorization path in the optimizer. any config diffs in rollout?
alice: rollout changed tokenizer shard count from 6 -> 4 to reduce memory footprint. maybe that reduced capacity under prefill spikes.
nora: suggest two quick actions: 1) pause kv-prefill and synth warmup, 2) revert tokenizer shard count to 6 for canary namespace and run a 1% canary to validate.
ram: +1. re-sharding to more pods is quick and should relieve CPU. i'll prepare the config flip.
deploy-bot: ACTION: prefill paused for rollout/2026-12-tokenizer-optim by nora at 3001112300
docs: updating release notes: "Hold - paused prefill due to tokenizer CPU spikes during warmup; reverting shard config in canary and running low-traffic canary". linking ENGREL-1407.
sre-oncall: plan: flip shard count in canary to 6, run 1% canary with a paced prefill for 20m. if stable, resume gradual warmup; if not, pin tokenizer change to next cycle and rollback to previous config.
ram: config flip applied in canary at 3001112355. starting canary smoke now.
sre-oncall: p95 trending down to 130ms after flip, tokenizer CPU back to ~30% on canary pods. will monitor for 20m and post traces.
alice: thanks. hold rollout and follow ENGREL-1407 for postmortem if needed. I'll notify product so they don't misinterpret the telemetry spike. :thumbsup:
